items.item_text: 01. The information provided in your application must support your selected answers in the supplemental questions. The information you provide will be verified and documentation may be required. Please be as honest and accurate as possible. You may be asked to demonstrate your knowledge and skills in a work sample or during an interview. By completing this supplemental questionnaire you are attesting that the information you have provided is accurate. Any misstatements, omissions, or falsification of information may eliminate you from consideration or result in dismissal. Options: Yes, I understand and agree | No, I do not agree

02. Which statement below best describes the highest level of education you have completed? Options: Some High School | High school graduate, diploma or the equivalent (GED) | Some college (less than 60 units) | Associate degree or at least 60 semester units | Bachelor's degree | Master's degree | Professional degree | Doctorate degree
03. If you indicated a some college or higher in the question above, please indicate the field of study:

04. How many years of full-time experience do you have working with ADOLESCENTS OR YOUNG ADULTS IN STRUCTURED SETTINGS, INCLUDING EXPERIENCE PERFORMING CAMPUS SECURITY OR RELATED SECURITY DUTIES? Options: No experience | Less than 1 year | 1 year but less than 2 years | 2 years but less than 3 years | 3 years but less than 4 years | 4 years but less than 5 years | 5 years or more

05. Based on your campus security experience, please provide details for your MOST RELEVANT positions. For each position, include: (a) Job Title: (b) Organization/Agency Name: (c) Key Relevant Duties: (d) Employment Period: (From MM/YYYY to MM/YYYY) If you have no relevant experience in this area, enter "N/A."

06. Please indicate the setting(s) in which you have gained your security, law enforcement, or safety management experience (check all that apply): Options: K-12 educational settings | Higher education (college/university) | Law enforcement agency (city, county, state, federal) | Private security | Other | No experience in this field
07. Do you possess a valid SB 1626/SB 390 School Security Guard Training certification? Options: Yes | No

08. Describe the most challenging security incident you have personally led on a school campus or in a similar environment. What was happening, what decisions did you make in the moment, how did you direct others, and what was the outcome? (Limit your response to 300 words or less.)

Patrols and monitors campus facilities, grounds, and events during assigned hours, including evenings, to promote a safe and secure learning environment; prepares and maintains required security-related reports and documentation.
Observes and patrols campus areas including hallways, restrooms, parking lots, and perimeter areas to identify potential safety issues or policy violations
Responds to and assists in resolving student behavioral incidents, conflicts, and emergencies, prioritizing de-escalation and conflict resolution strategies in accordance with district policy.
Assists school authorities in addressing unauthorized persons on campus and students leaving campus without permission
Assists in conducting searches of students or belongings when directed by administration, ensuring compliance with district protocols
Facilitates student check-in and tardy procedures using designated electronic or manual systems to track late arrivals and issue passes
Coordinates with administration and law enforcement agencies during investigations of illegal or anti-social activities
Addresses vaping, substance use, bullying, and other student conduct issues through intervention, documentation, and referral to appropriate personnel
Utilizes security tools and equipment including radios, surveillance systems, golf carts, and detection devices
Assists with crowd control at athletic events, dances, graduations, and other school functions
Provides transportation assistance to students, staff, and parents in district approved vehicles across campus and throughout the district as needed
Reports and documents graffiti, vandalism, or other property damage, and assists administrators in identifying and addressing responsible parties
Monitors and reports maintenance or safety hazards to appropriate personnel
Builds positive rapport with students to encourage compliance and create an approachable security presence
Responds to medical emergencies and provides emergency first aid and CPR within the scope of training and certification, while alerting appropriate medical personnel
Assists with emergency management operations and participates in campus safety events, programs, and related activities as assigned
Performs related duties as assigned
De-escalation and conflict resolution techniques
Analyze situations quickly and adopt effective courses of action while maintaining student safety
Adolescent behavior and development
Build positive relationships with students while maintaining appropriate authority
Campus safety and security procedures
De-escalate tense situations and resolve conflicts peacefully
Legal requirements related to student searches and rights
Safely intervene in physical altercations when necessary
District organization, operations, policies, and objectives
Maintain confidentiality regarding sensitive student and security information
Laws, rules, and regulations related to campus security
Remain calm and professional under pressure and in crisis situations and maintain emotional regulation during high-stress situations and traumatic incidents.
Emergency response procedures including crisis intervention
Learn, interpret, apply, and explain laws, policies, procedures, rules and regulations
Drug identification and detection procedures
Observe health and safety regulations and maintain personal safety awareness
Technology systems used for campus security (surveillance cameras, detection devices, communication equipment)
Maintain physical and emotional stamina during extended outdoor work in various weather conditions
Basic record-keeping and report writing techniques
Model communications and interactions that respect and include all individuals and their languages, abilities, religions, and cultures
Fundamental concepts of employment laws, codes, and regulations, including EEO, FLSA, FMLA, and Cal/OSHA and applicable provisions of collective bargaining agreements
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing with students, staff, parents, and law enforcement
Operate security equipment including radios, surveillance systems, and detection devices
Work independently with minimal supervision while maintaining accountability
Safely operate a district approved vehicle across campus and throughout the district as needed.
